newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil set to drift lower into the New Year.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil set to drift lower into the New Year.

text.p: Palm oil prices look set to drift lower in the coming months unless there is some unexpected news, European traders said.
"At the moment the market is going nowhere ahead of the USDA report on Friday and the PORLA data which is due for release next Tuesday," said a trader.
And unless either of these reports contains some unexpected news traders expect palm oil prices to continue to drift lower.
"We expect the PORLA stock data to be about in line with Ivan Wong's lastest estimate," said one trader.
On Tuesday Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong released his latest estimate which put local palmoil output during September at 843,000 tonnes, four percent up from August.
Wong put palm oil stocks at 905,000 tonnes, against offical figures of 800,893 tonnes at end-August.
Exports were put at 645,000 tonnes against 638,601 tonnes in August.
India's palm olein imports have declined in recent weeks despite a surge in demand ahead of the festival season as the local edible oil harvest starts to arrive.
"India is out of the market for now and we are unlikely to see Pakistan for sometime which takes two of the major buyers out of the market," said a trader.
Traders in Malaysia are "hoping or praying" for an increase in demand from China but Europe traders doubt this will happen.
"China did buy some extra palm oil in drums last month when the price of olein dipped but they are not likely to buy any large tonnages at this time of year," said one.
"We don't expect China to buy any more palm oil than they already are in coming months, mainly because during the winter season they prefered to buy soft oils," said a Singapore based trader.
During the past week crude palm oil asking prices in Europe have dropped by $10 a tonne with Nov offered at $542.50 on Tuesday against $552.50 last week.
Palm oil olein was unchanged at $535 a tonne for Nov/Dec.

Coconut oil prices have hardly moved during the past week with Oct/Nov offered at $735 a tonne at Tuesday's close, unchanged from this time last week, despite delays to the copra harvest in the Phippines.
Soft oils have drifed lower as Chicago futures eased under pressure from the soybean harvest.
But tight supplies and some concern over modified soybeans in parts of northern Europe have kept rape oil at a four to five guilders preimum over soy oil, while trade has been slow.
Dutch/EU rape oil was offered at 97.50 guilders for Nov/Jan at Tuesday's close against 99.50 last week while Dutch soy oil sellers were at 92.75 guilders against 94 guilders for the same positions.
